gender_patterns.rule_detail: nominalized adjective (superlative) used as abstract noun
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Nominalized adjectives referring to abstract concepts are neuter.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: nouns ending in -er are often masculine (especially agents or tools)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Nouns ending in -er are often masculine, especially for tools and agents.
Compound word: derived from 'der Tee', so masculine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun, gender from last component: Medizin (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: In compounds, the last noun determines the gender: Medizin is feminine → die Allgemeinmedizin

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun, gender from last part 'Bad' (neuter)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take gender from the last part: das Bad, so das Schwimmbad.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound noun: gender from last element 'Reportage' (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last part; here Reportage is feminine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun taking gender of last part: 'Referat' (neuter)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last element; 'Referat' is neuter (often the ending -at indicates neuter loanwords)

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun; gender from last element Arzt (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound noun: der Frauenarzt (der Arzt). Most compound nouns take the gender of the final element.
Language names ending in -isch are neuter, e.g., das Französisch, das Englisch

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound: last noun determines gender (Artikel is masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: In compound nouns, the last part determines the gender. Here 'Artikel' is masculine, so 'Frageartikel' is masculine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound: Frage + Bogen; gender from last element 'Bogen' (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last element. Bogen is masculine (der Bogen), so Fragebogen is der.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun; gender from last component Heilkunde (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound words take the gender of the last component. Heilkunde is feminine.
Most nouns ending in -e are feminine (e.g., die Lampe, die Sekunde), but there are some common masculine exceptions.
Words ending in -in are feminine and often denote female professionals.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound: gender determined by last element 'Tipp' (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: The gender of a compound noun is determined by the final word (here 'der Tipp').

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun, gender determined by the base word (Angebot, das)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last component (here, das Angebot)
Greek loanwords ending in -e are usually feminine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound noun, gender from last component 'Sprache' (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last component. 'Sprache' is feminine, so 'Fremdsprache' is feminine.
Many abstract nouns ending in -e derived from adjectives are feminine.
Male nationalities are generally masculine and follow the weak declension, adding -n in plural.
Words ending in -ion are typically feminine

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun: gender determined by last element (Mitarbeiter, masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last part: der Mitarbeiter, so der Service-Mitarbeiter. Plural often same as last part: die Service-Mitarbeiter.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound word, gender from last part Anzeige
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound word: gender determined by last part 'Anzeige' (die). Most words ending in -e are feminine.
Many feminine nouns end in -e, like die Lampe or die Sprache.
Many nouns ending in -nd are masculine, like der Freund, der Feind, der Grund.
Gender from 'der Kurs' (the course); many compound nouns take the gender of the last part.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound: gender determined by last component (das Büfett)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last part. Since 'Büfett' is neuter (das), the whole word is neuter.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: feminine because last part is feminine (-in suffix)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound noun: Fremdsprachen + Sekretärin. Gender determined by the last element 'Sekretärin' (feminine, -in suffix). Plural: -nen.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound with root 'Gebot' (neuter), so the compound is neuter.
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound words take the gender of the last element; since 'Gebot' is neuter, 'Angebot' is also neuter.
Compound word: gender is determined by the last part 'Kraft' (feminine)

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound word, gender from last component 'Hof' (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound noun: gender determined by the last part 'Hof' (der Hof → der Friedhof). Plural: Friedhöfe.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Feminine loanword, possibly influenced by 'die Karte'
gender_patterns.learner_hint: English loanword; feminine gender (associate with 'die Karte' for map).

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun: gender determined by last element 'Punkt'
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound noun: gender from last part, 'der Punkt' -> masculine

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound: gender determined by last element (Party)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last element. 'Party' is feminine in German (loanwords ending in -y are often feminine).
Compound nouns: gender is determined by the last part. 'Schnitt' is masculine, so 'Abschnitt' is masculine.
Loanword, often masculine. Plural: Skier or Ski.
Compounds take the gender of the last component; 'Board' is neuter.
Compound of 'mit' and 'Arbeit' (feminine), so also feminine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: compound noun: gender from last component Feier (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last part: die Feier.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun; gender from the last element 'Formular'
gender_patterns.learner_hint: The gender of compound nouns is determined by the last element. 'Formular' is neuter, so 'Anmeldeformular' is neuter.
As an English loanword, Smartphone is neuter (das). Plural: Smartphones.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound: gender determined by last component 'Stelle' (feminine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Führerscheinstelle is a compound noun; the last part 'Stelle' is feminine, so the whole word is feminine. Plural: Führerscheinstellen.
Many nouns with the prefix 'Ab-' are masculine, e.g. der Abschied, der Abflug, der Abgang.
Words ending in -ung are always feminine

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun; gender from last element 'Platz' (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound noun; gender derived from the final element Platz (masculine)
Most country names are neuter.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun, gender determined by last component 'Spiel' (neuter)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last component. 'Spiel' is neuter (das Spiel), so 'Fußballspiel' is das.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound: gender determined by the last part 'Leiter' (masculine)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last word. Since 'Leiter' is masculine, 'Abteilungsleiter' is masculine.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun: gender determined by last component 'Spiel' (neuter)
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last component. Since 'Spiel' is neuter, the whole word is neuter.

gender_patterns.rule_detail: Compound noun, gender determined by the final component 'Stadion' (neuter).
gender_patterns.learner_hint: Compound nouns take the gender of the last component. 'Stadion' is neuter, so 'Fußballstadion' is neuter.
